body:
### What happened? There is a bug in `kubelet` `startupProbe` if sidecar container is configured. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.32/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L249 The worker's decision to continue (return true) or stop (return false) is based only on the pod's restart policy, not the containers (sidecar have restartPolicy:Always) This can lead to a racing condition if the sidecar container fails at the first time and prober incorrectly exits: If sidecar container restarted with no problem at second attempt, startupProbe will never run again. This leads kubelet to think the initContainer never successfully initialized. There is another bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 the probe can possibly get recreated here. However if there are more than one containers has startup probes, and the first container has a running probe, it will skip other containers (because of an early`return`). As a result, reproduction requires at least 2 startup probes. With the example in the "How to reproduce", the `main-container` is stuck in Initializing state. kubectl desribe pod
``` $ kubectl describe pod init-probe-bug-repro Name: init-probe-bug-repro Namespace: default Priority: 0 Service Account: default Node: gke-cluster-1-pool-3-7b56b326-2rxq/10.128.0.96 Start Time: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 23:38:27 +0000 Labels: Annotations: Status: Pending IP: 10.112.2.93 IPs: IP: 10.112.2.93 Init Containers: buggy-init-container: Container ID: containerd://5c44b517ecfe0d162a31759d1a7f2399c1954d3d80c3225a0d8bf24d0982e952 Image: busybox Image ID: docker.io/library/busybox@sha256:f85340bf132ae937d2c2a763b8335c9bab35d6e8293f70f606b9c6178d84f42b Port: Host Port: Command: sh -c if [ ! -f /work/first_run_done ]; then echo "First run: creating marker and exiting with 1." touch /work/first_run_done exit 1 else echo "Second run: marker found. Timeline T=0s: The buggy-init-container starts. The prober creates a worker for it, which immediately begins its initialDelaySeconds: 10 wait. T=0.1s: The container's command runs, creates the /work/first_run_done file, and exits with code 1. The container is now in a Terminated state. T=0.1s to T=5s: The probe worker is still waiting for its initial delay to expire. It has not run a single probe. T=5s: The worker's delay is over, and it runs doProbe for the first time. It sees that the container is Terminated. The onHold flag is false because a probe has never completed. It proceeds to the check: if c.State.Running == nil. This is true. It executes the faulty return logic: return c.State.Terminated == nil || w.pod.Spec.RestartPolicy != v1.RestartPolicyNever. Since the pod's RestartPolicy is Never, this evaluates to false, and the probe worker terminates itself. Meanwhile: `kubelet` sees the terminated init container and, honoring its restartPolicy: Always, starts a new instance of it. The syncloop will attempt to recreate the probe. However due to the bug in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/prober/prober_manager.go#L194 , the loop will `return` early because the main container's probe already exists, it fails to check the initContainer's probe. Result: The new container instance starts, but its probe worker is gone. No new worker is created. The Kubelet sees a running container with a startup probe but not have a successful ran, assuming it's not ready. The main-container never starts. ### What did you expect to happen? startupProbe should honor the container's restartPolicy. The startupProbe should continue to probe even if the sidecar container has failed initially and restarts. The main container should eventually run if the sidecar container eventually start up healthy. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? ``` apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: init-probe-bug-repro spec: # The Pod's restart policy is Never, a key condition for the bug. restartPolicy: Never volumes: - name: workdir emptyDir: {} initContainers: - name: buggy-init-container image: busybox # The container's restart policy is Always. restartPolicy: Always volumeMounts: - name: workdir mountPath: /work # This command fails very quickly on the first run. command: - sh - -c - | if [ ! -f /work/first_run_done ]; then echo "First run: creating marker and exiting with 1." touch /work/first_run_done exit 1 else echo "Second run: marker found. Running as a sidecar." sleep infinity fi startupProbe: # This delay MUST be long enough for the first container instance # to start, run its command, and terminate. initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 2 failureThreshold: 3 # The probe command itself is irrelevant, as it will never be run # by the first worker. exec: command: ["/bin/true"] containers: - name: main-container image: registry.k8s.io/pause # Added a startupProbe to the main container. startupProbe: initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 5 exec: command: ["/bin/true"] ``` ### Anything else we need to know? _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
``` $ kubectl version Client Version: v1.32.4-dispatcher Kustomize Version: v5.5.0 Server Version: v1.32.2-gke.1297002 ```
